item.title: Who will lead the WHO?
item.description:
Former health ministers, serving WHO regional directors and senior health-policy officials have entered the race to succeed Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus as the agency confronts acute financial and geopolitical pressures.
The contest to lead the World Health Organization (WHO) from August 2027 has taken shape, with member states nominating seven candidates for the top post at the United Nations’ health agency.
The field includes two serving WHO regional directors, a former Qatari health minister, Indonesia’s current health minister, a Spanish physician and senior WHO official, a Chinese health-policy administrator, and an Armenian cancer specialist nominated by Botswana.
The WHO announced the candidates on October 29.
The contest will help determine the agency’s direction at a time of mounting pressure over global health financing, pandemic preparedness, access to care and international cooperation.
The nominees are Dr Hanan Mohammed Al-Kuwari of Qatar, Dr Hanan Balkhy of Saudi Arabia, Dr Hans Henri P Kluge of Belgium, Dr María P Neira of Spain, Budi Gunadi Sadikin of Indonesia, Dr Li Song of China, and Dr Gevorg Tamamyan, nominated by Botswana.
However, Dr Hanan Balkhy, WHO regional director for the Eastern Mediterranean, and Dr Hans Henri P Kluge, WHO regional director for Europe, have both temporarily stepped away from their regional duties while campaigning for the director-general position.
The next director-general will succeed Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, whose second term ends on August 15, 2027.
The successor will assume office the following day.
Dr Hanan Mohammed Al-Kuwari (Qatar) brings extensive experience in health-system management and public administration.
She served as Qatar’s minister of public health from 2016 to 2024 and led Hamad Medical Corporation, the country’s largest public healthcare provider, from 2007 to 2024.
She holds a PhD in healthcare management from Brunel University in the United Kingdom and has served on the WHO Executive Board, chairing it in 2023–24.
After leaving the ministry, she became an adviser to Qatar’s prime minister on public health affairs.
Her candidacy draws on experience managing a national health system and engaging with international health governance.
Dr Hanan Balkhy (Saudi Arabia) has been WHO regional director for the Eastern Mediterranean since February 2024.
A paediatrician specialising in infectious diseases, she previously served as WHO assistant director-general for antimicrobial resistance from 2019 to 2024.
Her expertise spans infection prevention, antimicrobial resistance and public health emergencies.
Her current position gives her direct oversight of WHO operations in a region marked by conflict, humanitarian crises and persistent health-system fragility.
Dr Hans Henri P Kluge (Belgium) has served as WHO regional director for Europe since 2020.
A family physician with more than three decades of experience in public health and international health programmes, he previously worked with Médecins Sans Frontières and on WHO initiatives addressing tuberculosis and HIV.
From 2009 to 2020, he headed the Division of Health Systems and Public Health at WHO Europe.
He guided the region through the Covid-19 pandemic and subsequent public health emergencies, giving him extensive institutional experience.
Dr María P Neira (Spain) is a physician and senior WHO official whose work has centred on environmental health, climate change and public health policy.
She has served as director of WHO’s work on environment, climate change and health, and previously held senior public health positions in Spain, including vice-minister of health and consumer affairs.
Her career also includes humanitarian field service with Médecins Sans Frontières.
She is closely associated with climate-related health risks, pollution and the environmental determinants of disease.
Budi Gunadi Sadikin (Indonesia) has been Indonesia’s health minister since December 2020.
Unlike most of his rivals, he does not have a clinical medical background.
A former banker and corporate executive, he has been closely involved in Indonesia’s Covid-19 response and national vaccination programme, as well as healthcare financing and health-system reform.
His candidacy offers a managerial and economic perspective as the WHO faces pressure to secure its financial sustainability.
Dr Li Song (China) is a senior public health official with extensive experience in health administration and policy.
She previously headed the women and children’s health department of China’s National Health Commission and has worked on maternal and child health policy and international cooperation.
Her career includes involvement in China’s responses to major public health emergencies, including SARS and Covid-19.
She currently serves as a secretary of the secretariat of the All-China Women’s Federation.
Her nomination comes as Beijing seeks a larger role in multilateral institutions and global health governance.
Dr Gevorg Tamamyan (nominated by Botswana) is an Armenian paediatric oncologist, professor and medical researcher specialising in cancer and blood disorders.
He leads the Pediatric Cancer and Blood Disorders Center of Armenia and heads the Department of Pediatric Oncology and Hematology at Yerevan State Medical University.
He has also held leadership roles in international paediatric oncology.
His nomination by Botswana is notable because he is not a national of the country proposing him.
WHO rules allow a member state to nominate a candidate who is not its citizen.
His clinical background brings a focus on cancer care and access to health services to a field otherwise dominated by senior administrators and government officials.
The election arrives at a difficult moment for the WHO, which faces financial constraints, declining international health spending and questions over how it can sustain its global programmes while responding to emergencies.
The withdrawal of the United States from the agency, together with a broader contraction in global health financing, has deepened concerns about its future.
The next director-general will be expected to stabilise the organisation’s finances, preserve cooperation among member states and strengthen its credibility in global health decision-making.
The candidates’ backgrounds point to differing priorities, from health-system management and emergency response to climate and environmental health, financing and clinical care.
The nominations alone, however, do not reveal a clear frontrunner.
The outcome will depend on diplomatic engagement and the support each candidate can secure among member states through the formal election process.
November 18–19, 2026: The seven candidates will participate in the first candidates’ forum at WHO Headquarters in Geneva, engaging member states and associate members. The forum will be publicly webcast in the organisation’s six official languages.
January 2027: At its 160th session, the WHO Executive Board will shortlist five candidates, interview them and nominate up to three for consideration by the World Health Assembly.
March 15, 2027: A second candidates’ forum will be held for those nominated by the Executive Board.
May 2027: The World Health Assembly, the WHO’s decision-making body comprising delegations from all member states, will appoint the new director-general at its 80th session.

item.title: Titumir: Bangladesh aims to become global manufacturing hub, export gateway
item.description:
Bangladesh has set a target of becoming a global manufacturing hub and export gateway to accelerate its economic development, Prime Minister’s Adviser on Finance and Planning Prof Dr Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir said.
He made the remarks while addressing the inaugural session of the 29th Sustainable Development Conference, organised by the Sustainable Development Policy Institute (SDPI) in Islamabad, Pakistan, as the guest of honour on Monday, according to a press release issued by the Bangladesh High Commission in Islamabad on Tuesday.
Titumir said cooperation between Bangladesh and Pakistan could establish a new model of regional partnership. He proposed establishing integrated production networks connecting South Asia, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and North Africa.
He emphasised that developing countries should attract investments that build domestic capabilities, facilitate technology transfer and create employment opportunities.
The adviser also said Bangladesh plans to increase public spending on education from around two percent of GDP at present to 5% by 2030.
He said Bangladesh was working to develop stronger production networks with South Asian countries. Such initiatives could help restore normal production activities following prolonged disruptions in global manufacturing structures and contribute to people-centred and sustainable development across the region.
Referring to the ongoing global economic slowdown, he said the government was implementing social protection programmes, including Family Cards and Farmer Cards, to promote balanced development and support vulnerable communities.
He expressed optimism that these initiatives would help Bangladesh overcome prolonged economic challenges and poverty stemming from war, energy shortages and the misgovernance of the previous government.
Pakistan’s Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Prof Ahsan Iqbal delivered the keynote address at the conference.
The four-day conference features around 50 panel and plenary sessions, bringing together more than 300 development experts and prominent figures from political and social sectors from different countries. More than 100 women are among the participants.
Delegates from South Asia, Southeast Asia, China and other parts of the world are attending the conference.
Following the conference, Titumir visited the newly constructed Bangladesh Chancery Complex in Islamabad and exchanged greetings with officials and employees of the Bangladesh High Commission.
He also planted a sapling on the chancery premises.
During his visit, the adviser held separate meetings with Pakistan’s Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb, Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Prof Ahsan Iqbal, Federal Minister for Energy Ali Pervaiz Malik and Prime Minister’s Adviser on Industries and Production Haroon Akhtar Khan.
The meetings discussed opportunities for exchanging experiences and strengthening mutual cooperation to address challenges in areas of common interest.

item.title: At least 50 police injured in Ashulia worker clashes
item.description:
Garment workers continued their protests in Ashulia, Savar, on Tuesday, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000 and other benefits, triggering clashes with police at several points along the Abdullahpur-Baipail road. At least 50 police personnel have been injured in the clashes so far.
Clashes, chases and counter-chases, and brickbat throwing were reported at different locations from the morning. Police fired tear gas to disperse the protesters and bring the situation under control.
Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of police (SP) of Ashulia Industrial Police-1, said attempts were being made to divert the workers' movement and destabilise the situation.
"At least 50 police personnel have been injured at different locations on Tuesday while trying to bring the situation under control," he said.
Meanwhile, more than 100 garment factories had declared general holidays by Tuesday afternoon. However, production continued at most factories in the industrial area, according to industrial police.
According to Ashulia Industrial Police, workers reported to factories along the Abdullahpur-Baipail road at their scheduled time in the morning. Workers at several factories stopped working and staged sit-ins, prompting the authorities to declare holidays at more than 100 factories.
Around 8:30am, workers set tyres on fire at several points on the road in front of a Ha-Meem Group factory in the Narsinghpur area. Clashes and exchanges of brickbats between workers and police followed.
Police fired tear gas to disperse the protesters, who later took positions in various alleys in the area.
Around 10:00am, workers blocked the Abdullahpur-Baipail road in the Unique area and staged demonstrations.
A visit to Nishchintapur found workers and police facing each other in an alley beside the Abdullahpur-Baipail road. Workers were seen throwing bricks and stones at police, while officers used loudspeakers to urge them to disperse.
Earlier, police had fired tear gas to clear the road after workers blocked it.
SP Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan said more than 100 factories had declared holidays amid the unrest.
He added that workers at around 20 to 25 factories had stopped working and were staying inside their workplaces.
However, he claimed that most workers wanted to continue working, but a group of outsiders was inciting some of them to leave factories after arriving for their morning shifts.
"We believe ordinary workers want to work and keep the factories running. However, a group, allegedly backed by outsiders, is trying to provoke workers arriving for their morning shifts and bring them out of factories. They are throwing bricks and stones in an attempt to destabilise the situation," he said.
Stating that industrial police were taking steps to ensure workers' safety, the SP said adequate security measures had been taken to allow them to work safely.
"However, workers at some factories have been forced to suspend operations for security reasons. Allegations that police are using force in this regard are not true," he added.

item.title: Dhaka Elevated Expressway to remain toll-free for six hours on Nov 7
item.description:
The Dhaka Elevated Expressway will remain toll-free for six hours on Saturday, marking National Revolution and Solidarity Day. All vehicles will be allowed to use the expressway free of charge from 6:00am to 12pm.
The Bangladesh Bridge Authority announced the decision in a press release on Tuesday.
According to the press release, the toll-free facility will apply to all vehicles using the expressway during the designated six-hour period.
Last year, the expressway was kept toll-free for four hours on December 25, when BNP Chairman and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman returned home from London after nearly 17 years. The BNP organised a public reception to mark his return.
The expressway also operated without toll collection for several days after toll plazas were damaged during the July Mass Uprising.
Built under a public-private partnership (PPP), the Dhaka Elevated Expressway was partially opened to traffic in September 2023. Currently, the operational section stretches from Kawla, near Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, to the FDC intersection in the capital. Vehicles are normally charged tolls for using the expressway.
Toll rates vary by vehicle category. Cars, taxis, sports utility vehicles (SUVs), microbuses with fewer than 16 seats and light trucks weighing less than three tonnes are charged Tk80.
Medium trucks with up to six wheels are charged Tk320, while trucks with more than six wheels pay Tk400. Buses with 16 or more seats are charged Tk160.
Rickshaws, motorcycles and auto-rickshaws are not allowed on the expressway.
The 19.73-kilometre expressway is designed to connect Kawla, near Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, with Kutubkhali near Jatrabari on the Dhaka-Chittagong Highway, passing through Tejgaon, Moghbazar and Kamalapur along the railway corridor.
However, construction of the full route is yet to be completed.
The project comprises two components: the main construction work and associated works.
The main construction component has an estimated cost of Tk8,940 crore, of which the government is contributing Tk2,413 crore, with the remaining amount being financed by the investor consortium.
A separate project covers land acquisition, rehabilitation of affected people and consultancy services, with its entire cost borne by the government. The estimated cost of this component is Tk4,917 crore.
The combined estimated cost of the two projects stands at Tk13,857 crore.
The project was initiated in 2009, and the construction agreement was signed in 2011. The construction period was initially set at three and a half years, but the project could not be completed within the stipulated timeframe.

item.title: Menzies pitches Dhaka aviation academy in bid for Third Terminal contract
item.description:
UK-based Menzies Aviation has proposed setting up a specialised aviation training academy in Dhaka as it competes for the second passenger ground-handling contract at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport’s Third Terminal.
The company says the academy, along with a proposed investment of over $12 million in the first year, could give it an edge over rivals Swissport, Çelebi Aviation and dnata.
Menzies plans to train local recruits in aircraft ground handling, aviation security, equipment operations, baggage management and safety procedures.
It also intends to partner with Bangladeshi universities and training institutions on qualifications and internships.
“We are planning to set up a training academy in Dhaka,” said John Henderson, the company’s senior vice president of operations.
“Bangladeshi workers will be able to work anywhere in our international network.”
Henderson said staff could be recruited and trained to international standards within three months of starting operations.
The academy could help build a skilled local workforce and reduce reliance on foreign technical experts.
Menzies estimates its Bangladesh operations could create more than 1,000 direct jobs, about 99% of them for Bangladeshis, and around 4,500 indirect jobs.
The investment would fund modern equipment, technology, infrastructure and workforce development.
The company operates at about 350 airports in 65 countries, handling roughly 1.6 million aircraft turnarounds and 2.4 million tonnes of cargo a year, according to its executives.
Menzies has also proposed digital baggage tracking and real-time operational monitoring.
It claims the first bag from a wide-body aircraft could be delivered within 10 to 15 minutes, and all bags within 40 minutes.
The company also plans to source and manufacture staff uniforms locally, benefiting the garment industry.
The academy and investment pledges remain at the proposal stage and will be implemented only if Menzies wins the contract.
Its advantage will ultimately depend on whether the promises translate into better workforce skills, baggage delivery, turnaround times, safety and reliability.
Former CAAB Chairman Air Vice Marshal (retd) Muhammad Mafidur Rahman has stressed the need for operators experienced in running complex airport systems.
Aviation analyst ATM Nazrul has argued that the choice should rest on competence, technology, operational capability and financial value.

Narayanganj garment workers clash with police over wage demand
item.description:
Garment workers clashed with police on the Dhaka-Narayanganj Link Road on Tuesday as protests demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000 entered their second day.
Workers hurled bricks and stones at police, who responded with batons and tear gas to bring the situation under control. Several people, including a police officer, were injured.
The clashes broke out around 4:45pm in the Jalkuri area of Siddhirganj.
According to police and local sources, workers began blocking the road and demonstrating in the Shibu Market area around 3pm. Police tried to stop them by setting up barricades, but the protesters broke through and took to the main road.
Some workers set fires at different points along the road and chanted slogans while carrying sticks, bringing traffic to a halt in the surrounding areas.
When police tried to calm the protesters, workers hurled bricks and stones at them. Police then charged batons and fired tear shells, triggering chases and counter-chases before the situation escalated into clashes.
Several garment workers and a police officer were injured. Their identities could not immediately be confirmed.
Mohammad Shahin Ahmed, president of the district unit of the Garment Workers Trade Union, said workers had blocked the road on Monday over their demand for a Tk30,000 minimum wage and resumed the protest on Tuesday as their demands remained unmet.
He said he was unaware of the injuries.
Narayanganj Additional Superintendent of Police Tarek Al Mehedi said protesters had thrown bricks and stones at police, prompting officers to fire tear gas to restore order.
Garment workers had blocked the same road on Monday over a five-point set of demands. The blockade halted traffic for nearly four hours from noon before workers withdrew around 4:15pm following assurances from the local lawmaker, district administration and police.
Their demands include setting the minimum monthly wage at Tk30,000, introducing rationing facilities at all garment factories, ensuring trade union rights, bringing those responsible for the deaths of workers, including Amzad Hossain Kamal, to justice, ending arbitrary layoffs and fully implementing labour laws.
Factory operations at Panchabati BSCIC Industrial Estate and Adamjee Export Processing Zone in Siddhirganj were normal on Tuesday morning, with workers reporting for duty.
However, tensions flared again after workers took to the streets in the Katherpul area around 3:15pm.
Following Monday’s blockade, Deputy Commissioner Raihan Kabir had announced the deployment of five platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) to strengthen security in the district. Three platoons were kept in reserve and two assigned to patrol.
Law enforcement personnel were deployed at the scene on Tuesday to bring the situation under control.

item.title: Dengue: 6 more die, 2,010 hospitalized in 24hrs
item.description:
Six more people died from dengue across the country in the 24 hours until 8:00am on Tuesday, while 2,010 new patients were hospitalised with the mosquito-borne disease.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) confirmed the figures in a press release issued on Tuesday.
Of the newly hospitalised patients, 943 were in Dhaka Division, 245 in Chittagong, 235 in Khulna, 219 each in Rajshahi and Barisal, 65 in Rangpur, 60 in Mymensingh and 24 in Sylhet.
Since the beginning of this year, a total of 140,909 people have been admitted to hospitals with dengue across the country, according to the DGHS.
Of them, 134,594 have recovered and been discharged, while 5,876 patients are currently receiving treatment at hospitals.
The dengue death toll this year has reached 439.

item.title: Exhibition marking Jail Killing Day postponed over security concerns
item.description:
The Liberation War Museum has postponed a special exhibition commemorating the four national leaders at the request of law enforcement agencies on Tuesday.
Mofidul Hoque, a trustee of the museum, said the decision to postpone the event was taken on Tuesday, following a request from law enforcement agencies citing security concerns.
The exhibition was scheduled to be inaugurated at 4pm on Tuesday at Gallery 6 on the museum's sixth floor. Waliul Islam, a former secretary who served in the wartime government, was scheduled to speak at the opening ceremony.
According to the invitation, the exhibition was organised to commemorate the contributions of the four national leaders, who played a significant role in the country's independence struggle and the Liberation War.
On November 3, 1975, the four leaders – Syed Nazrul Islam, acting president of the wartime Mujibnagar government; Tajuddin Ahmad, the country’s first prime minister; and cabinet members Captain M Mansur Ali and AHM Qamaruzzaman – who led Bangladesh's Liberation War, were killed inside Dhaka Central Jail.
The 15-day exhibition, titled “The Four National Leaders in the Independence Struggle,” was scheduled to run from November 3 to 17.
Officer-in-Charge of Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police station Monirul Islam told Dhaka Tribune that intelligence information had raised security concerns surrounding the event.
“After informing the organisers about the matter, they cancelled the programme,” he said.

item.title: Gazipur labour unrest leaves 30 injured, 7 arrested
item.description:
At least 30 people, including workers and police personnel, were injured in clashes between garment workers and police in Gazipur as workers took to the streets demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000.
Industrial police arrested seven people on charges of sabotage.
The clashes and chases took place in the Bhogra, Naojor, Mouchak and Palli Bidyut areas from around 9:30am until noon on Tuesday.
According to workers and industrial police, employees of Panasia Limited in Naojor came out of the factory around 9:30am and gathered on the western side of the Dhaka-Tangail Highway flyover. They later blocked the highway, bringing traffic to a standstill on both sides.
At the same time, workers of Bay Footwear in Konabari, Purvani in Mouchak, and Logos Apparels and ATS Apparels in Telichala stopped work and joined the protests, taking positions on the highway.
Police and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel, led by Gazipur Metropolitan Police (GMP) Deputy Commissioner (Crime and Operations) Mohammad Belayet Hossain, later fired tear gas shells and sound grenades to disperse the protesters. Traffic resumed after the situation came under control.
Meanwhile, workers from several factories blocked the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway in the Bhogra area around 9:30am, setting tyres on fire.
Industrial police, BGB, district police and metropolitan police personnel rushed to the scene and tried to defuse the situation through negotiations. However, protesters suddenly pelted police with bricks and stones, injuring several officers. Police later fired tear gas shells and charged batons to disperse the protesters.
Since Saturday, garment workers in several areas of Gazipur, including Chandra, Palli Bidyut, Mouchak, Safipur and Konabari in Kaliakair, have been staging demonstrations and blocking highways to press their demand for higher wages.
The protests have also seen incidents of vehicle vandalism and arson attacks on police boxes and vehicles. Several people, including police personnel and journalists, have been injured, while a factory warehouse was also set on fire.
Additional law enforcement personnel have been deployed at key points across the industrial zones to maintain order.
Police have filed three cases with Konabari, Basan and Kaliakair Police Stations over the incidents, implicating several thousand workers. Several people have also been arrested on allegations of participating in and instigating the unrest.
Gazipur Industrial Police Superintendent Amzad Hossain said at least 60 factories had announced closures for the day after 11am amid the labour unrest.
He said the seven people arrested on charges of sabotage were not factory workers.
The protests disrupted traffic on the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway from 9:30am and the Dhaka-Tangail Highway from 11:00am, causing severe suffering to commuters.
Traffic on the Dhaka-Tangail Highway returned to normal around 11:30am after protesters were cleared from the road. On the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway, traffic resumed around 12:30pm following a three-hour disruption.
Amzad said police had arrested seven people in connection with the unrest.
He added that earlier, around 7:45am, a group of workers had attempted to block the Dhaka-Tangail Highway in the Mouchak area of Kaliakair. Law enforcement personnel intervened and persuaded them to leave without any confrontation.
Around the same time, workers also attempted to block the highway at Palli Bidyut intersection in Kaliakair. Police and BGB personnel rushed to the spot and cleared the road.
GMP Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Belayet Hossain said he had visited several points along the highways since morning to speak with the workers.
"I went to Naojor, where garment workers had gathered. I spoke to them, and they left after the discussion. Workers have staged protests on various occasions, but this time the pattern is somewhat different. Everything seemed to be going smoothly when suddenly stones started being thrown. Someone is trying to exploit the situation to create an issue," he said.
He added that barricades erected in the Naojor and Bhogra bypass areas had been removed.

item.title: NBR: VAT collection growth to rebound in October
item.description:
VAT collection is expected to return to double-digit growth in October after a temporary decline caused by the shift to quarterly return submissions, said National Board of Revenue (NBR) chairman Ahsan Habib on Tuesday.
He said VAT collection had already recorded 23% year-on-year growth in October and could reach 30% as thousands of payment challans are entered into the system.
Meanwhile, income tax collection grew 14%, while customs revenue increased 16%, he said, describing the overall revenue collection trend as encouraging.
The NBR chairman made the comments at a reception program for the 45th batch of income tax cadre officers at the NBR headquarters in Dhaka's Agargaon, organized by the Bangladesh Civil Service (Taxation) Association.
He said VAT collection growth currently stood at minus 6.6% during the July-October period, largely due to the shift from monthly to quarterly VAT return submissions.
The deadline for submitting returns for the three months was initially October 15, which the NBR extended to October 25.
He said the entry of the resulting payment challans into the system was still underway.
The NBR chairman expressed confidence that VAT collection would return to its historical growth trajectory and achieve healthy double-digit growth.
In the first quarter of the current fiscal year, the revenue authority fell Tk41,879 crore short of its revenue target, as collection grew by less than 2% year-on-year, while VAT collection witnessed major negative growth.
Ahsan urged newly appointed revenue officials to prioritize tax collection and perform their duties honestly and sincerely.
"Remember, the ultimate output of the revenue department is to collect taxes. Your journey begins with a tax return and ends with an e-challan," he said.
Syed Mohidul Hasan, general secretary of the platform, also urged newly appointed tax officials to uphold integrity, ensure fair revenue collection and protect taxpayers' legitimate rights.
He encouraged them to learn from senior colleagues, take responsibility for their work and provide courteous, transparent and efficient services to taxpayers.
Kobir Uddin Mollah, vice president of the association, chaired the event.

item.title: CSOs urge stronger climate commitments, equitable action ahead of COP31
item.description:
Civil society organizations (CSOs) have called for equitable climate action, accessible climate finance and stronger global commitments ahead of the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31), urging world leaders to move beyond political pledges and deliver tangible results.
The call came at a national seminar titled “31st Conference of the Parties: Articulating CSOs’ Positions Together”, organized by the Center for Participatory Research and Development (CPRD) in collaboration with the Climate Justice Alliance–Bangladesh (CJA-B) at City Hotel in Dhaka on November 3.
Participants also presented a civil society position paper prepared by CPRD and CJA-B member organizations, outlining key demands for climate negotiations and the implementation of global climate commitments.
The priorities include aligning the third cycle of Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) with the 1.5°C temperature goal, accelerating the implementation of National Adaptation Plans (NAPs), strengthening arrangements to address loss and damage, and ensuring adequate and accessible climate finance under the New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG) and Article 9 of the Paris Agreement.
The discussions also emphasized implementing the outcomes of the first Global Stocktake, safeguarding the environmental integrity of Article 6 carbon market mechanisms, and advancing an inclusive, rights-based and adequately financed Just Transition Mechanism.
In his welcome address, CPRD Chief Executive and CJA-B Coordinator Md Shamsuddoha called for a unified civil society voice to strengthen Bangladesh’s negotiating position at COP31.
Highlighting the growing risks faced by frontline communities, he stressed the need for stronger government–CSO collaboration to ensure climate commitments translate into concrete action grounded in equity and climate justice.
Presenting the alliance’s key positions and demands, Sheikh Nur Ataya Rabbi, manager of research and advocacy at CPRD, outlined the priorities developed by CJA-B and its partner organizations.
Representatives of alliance member organizations also shared their perspectives on the COP process, calling for climate outcomes that prioritize vulnerable communities, uphold rights and deliver meaningful progress on climate justice.
Those taking part included Nuzhat Jabin, partnership and strategy lead at Christian Aid Bangladesh; Shahnawaz Whara, program coordinator for climate adaptation and resilience at Concern Worldwide; Tazeen Hossain, head of programs at Educo; Farhana Afroz, program director at HELVETAS; ASM Rahmat Ullah Bhuiyan, deputy country director of Save the Children Bangladesh; Rabeya Begum, executive director of SDS; Mohsin Ali, executive director of WAVE Foundation; Partha Hefaz Sheikh, director of program and policy advocacy; and Mohammad Shahjahan, director of YPSA.
Expert reflections on the civil society position paper were delivered by Professor Niaz Ahmed Khan, former vice-chancellor of the University of Dhaka; Dr Shah Abdul Saadi, joint secretary at the Economic Relations Division (ERD); and Dr M Asaduzzaman, former research director at the Bangladesh Institute of Development Studies (BIDS).
Speaking as a guest speaker, ERD Additional Secretary AKM Sohel highlighted the role of civil society organizations in influencing international climate negotiations and shaping global climate positions.
He urged CSOs to strengthen their advocacy on climate finance and just transition, while recognizing CPRD and CJA-B’s publications and activities as useful resources for negotiators and climate activists.
Calling for concrete implementation rather than political rhetoric, he said COP31 and the international community must deliver “not a political package, but a package of action and implementation.”
Barrister Jahrat Adib Chowdhury, MP, chair of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, highlighted the role of parliament and diplomacy in advancing Bangladesh’s climate priorities.
She stressed the importance of climate justice, protecting the interests of climate-vulnerable countries and translating international commitments into meaningful action.
Emphasizing the need for evidence-based policymaking, she called for more research into climate change and Bangladesh’s vulnerabilities, saying, “All our arguments need to be driven by data.”
She also underscored the importance of collaboration and knowledge-sharing between civil society organizations and policymakers in strengthening Bangladesh’s position in international negotiations.
Delivering the chief guest’s address, State Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Sheikh Faridul Islam, MP, reaffirmed the government’s commitment to addressing climate change and protecting the environment.
“The government’s top priorities are to protect the environment and address the adverse impacts of climate change,” he said.
The state minister highlighted the importance of climate adaptation, resilience-building, adequate climate finance and effective measures to address loss and damage.
Outlining ongoing government initiatives, he said Bangladesh was promoting solar energy, planting trees to absorb carbon and undertaking mangrove plantation initiatives to protect coastal areas.
“We are not waiting for external support to take action, although we must need financial and technical assistance to protect our people,” he said, referring to the country’s efforts to strengthen environmental protection and coastal resilience.
He also emphasized constructive engagement between the government and civil society in articulating Bangladesh’s priorities and building a stronger collective voice ahead of COP31.
The seminar concluded with renewed calls for international climate commitments to be backed by adequate financing, effective implementation and greater accountability, with particular attention to the needs of countries and communities most vulnerable to climate change.

item.title: How to maximize returns with 3-month savings certificates
item.description:
Do you want to keep your savings secure while earning regular profits? Then the "Three-Month Profit-Based Savings Certificate" could be an option.
Introduced nearly 28 years ago, the special feature of this savings certificate is that it can be purchased by Bangladeshi citizens from all professions and walks of life.
It also offers the opportunity to withdraw profits every three months against the investment.
Unlike the Family Savings Certificate (Poribar Sanchayapatra) and Pensioner Savings Certificate, it is not restricted to specific groups of people.
However, there are certain rules regarding investment limits, profit rates, and purchasing procedures.
These savings certificates are available in denominations of Tk1 lakh, Tk2 lakh, Tk5 lakh, and Tk10 lakh.
They can be purchased from District Savings Offices, National Savings Special Bureaus, commercial banks, and post offices.
The tenure of this certificate is three years.
For investments up to Tk7.5 lakh, the profit rate upon maturity is 11.82%.
For investments exceeding that amount, the rate is 11.77%.
Encashing the certificate before maturity yields a relatively lower profit rate.
If excess profit has already been paid out, it will be adjusted against the principal amount.
An individual can invest a maximum of Tk30 lakh in a single name and Tk60 lakh in a joint name.
Additionally, various institutions and firms can purchase these savings certificates under specific conditions.
Eligibility
Bangladeshi citizens of all classes and professions can purchase these savings certificates.
In addition, under specific conditions, recognized provident funds, agricultural and farm-based income-generating institutions, organizations supporting autistic individuals, and registered shelters for distressed orphans and the elderly are eligible to invest.
Tax is deducted at source (TDS) from the profits of the savings certificate.
A tax of 10% is deducted if the investor has a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), and 15% if they do not have a TIN.
However, this withheld tax is no longer a final tax liability. During the submission of income tax returns, there is an opportunity to adjust the tax deducted at source according to the rules.
One of the main advantages of this savings certificate is the opportunity to collect profits every three months.
Additionally, nominees can be appointed. In the event of the purchaser’s death, the nominee can either encash the certificate to withdraw the funds or continue collecting profits every three months until maturity.
Furthermore, investors can utilize the automatic reinvestment facility by contacting the issuing office before maturity.

item.title: Kane would trade Ballon d'Or for Champions League trophy
item.description:
Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane said Monday he would trade that accolade for the Champions League trophy, ahead of Bayern Munich's visit to face Atletico Madrid.
Kane was named the world's best player last week, beating superstars Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to the prestigious award.
However the England international said the reason he plays the game is to enjoy success with his team-mates.
"Team trophies are why we play football. The team aspect of our sport is really, really important," Kane told reporters in the Spanish capital.
"The Ballon d'Or last week was one of the best feelings I've had in my life and my career... but to have moments with the team, celebrations with the club, to be able to lift the Champions League with Bayern would be an incredible feeling.
"Of course the Ballon d'Or is a highlight, it puts me on an even bigger level, but you want to have these big finals, the Champions League, having that feeling of emotion with your team-mates as well.
"I would choose the Champions League, but I have the opportunity to do both -- let's see what happens."
The 33-year-old striker was hailed by Atletico coach Diego Simeone as an "incredible player" and "very good for football", before Tuesday's match.
"I'd like to thank Diego Simeone, who is one of the best coaches of this era," said Kane.
"I'm proud to receive praise from someone like him. Winning the Ballon d'Or was a huge achievement for me –- I've had to overcome many challenges in my career, some people didn't think I'd get this far... but Simeone will do everything he can to stop me and the team tomorrow."
Bayern have only won one of their first three league phase games, with draws against Arsenal and Viking.
Kane suffered defeat in Atletico's Metropolitano stadium in 2019 when playing in the Champions League final for Tottenham against Liverpool. It is also the venue for this season's final.
"You have good memories in stadiums, sometimes you don't -- hopefully we can have a good memory tomorrow," added Kane.
"I play again here next week with England against Spain, and then hopefully at the end of the year we're back again for the Champions League final.
"So I have a chance and we have a chance to erase that painful memory from 2019 for sure, and that's what you can do in life and football, just take the next opportunity."
- New deal -
Kane also confirmed he was close to sealing a new deal to keep him in Munich for the foreseeable future.
"I'd say it's more days (than weeks)... we're extremely close now," said Kane, with his current contract expiring in June 2027.
Bayern assistant coach Aaron Danks, who is standing in for Vincent Kompany in the Belgian's absence with illness, said Michael Olise and Manuel Neuer were available after injury issues.
Kompany was released after five days in hospital last week following a collapse in training and subsequent diagnosis of meningeal irritation.
"The most important part of my role in Vinny's absence is to protect everything that we've built over the last two and a half years," said Danks.
"It's to protect the processes that we've put in place, to protect the identity of the team. So no, not too much will change."

item.title: From Camp Nou holiday tour to UCL for Villa's McGinn
item.description:
Aston Villa captain John McGinn will lead his team out at Camp Nou to face Barcelona in the Champions League on Tuesday, having only ever visited the stadium once before on holiday.
The Scotland international said he was excited to take on the Spanish champions, with Villa facing Barca for the first time in over 40 years.
"(I've been here) once -- I checked yesterday because I used to go on holidays at Port Aventura (theme park) in Salou," McGinn told reporters Monday.
"I was here for the stadium tour the day Ricardo Quaresma signed for Barcelona (in July 2003), I was eight years old...
"I've never been since but tomorrow night I'll be excited to represent Aston Villa on the biggest stage."
The midfielder said Villa reaching Europe's top competition allowed him to keep fulfilling his childhood dreams.
"I am 32 years old, but the trajectory of this club is allowing me to dream the same way I have dreamed since I was 9, 10, 11, to play in front of the biggest crowds, in the biggest arenas, and obviously this is a very historic stadium," continued McGinn.
"But what the club are trying to do now is make this normal, make this a yearly experience, and make Aston Villa compete with the best in England and the best in Europe.
"It is a pleasure to be on this journey with the supporters. I am sure they will enjoy tonight and tomorrow, but as a professional, we only enjoy the experience if we have three points."
So far Villa have three victories from three league phase games, defeating Viking, Fenerbahce and Club Brugge.
Unai Emery, whose Paris Saint-Germain side were beaten 6-1 by Barcelona at Camp Nou in 2017 in a historic Champions League comeback known as the 'remontada', said Hansi Flick's side were one of the favourites to win the trophy.
"In that match I learned so, so much. One, the sports side, and another not a sports side. The necessity for VAR in that moment," said Emery.
Barca lost their previous European outing against PSG, and also lost against Real Madrid in La Liga.
"Barcelona are going to demand a lot from us, we have to be capable of adapting to that," continued Emery.
"It will be a different game to the PSG and Madrid games, and we have to play our own one."
